verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, “Depart, go up from here, you and the people that you have brought up out of the land of Egypt, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your offspring. ’
I will send an angel before you; and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
to a land flowing with milk and honey: for I will not go up among you, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way.”
When the people heard this evil news, they mourned: and no one put on his jewelry.

Yahweh said to Moses, “Tell the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go up into the middle of you for one moment, I would consume you. Therefore now take off your jewelry from you, that I may know what to do to you.’”
The children of Israel stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.

Now Moses used to take the tent and to pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp, and he called it “The Tent of Meeting.” Everyone who sought Yahweh went out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp.
When Moses went out to the Tent, that all the people rose up, and stood, everyone at their tent door, and watched Moses, until he had gone into the Tent.
When Moses entered into the Tent, the pillar of cloud descended, stood at the door of the Tent, and spoke with Moses.
All the people saw the pillar of cloud stand at the door of the Tent, and all the people rose up and worshiped, everyone at their tent door.
Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.

Moses said to Yahweh, “Behold, you tell me, ‘Bring up this people:’ and you haven’t let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’
Now therefore, if I have found favor in your sight, please show me now your way, that I may know you, so that I may find favor in your sight: and consider that this nation is your people.”
He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
He said to him, “If your presence doesn’t go with me, don’t carry us up from here.

For how would people know that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Isn’t it that you go with us, so that we are separated, I and your people, from all the people who are on the surface of the earth?”
Yahweh said to Moses, “I will do this thing also that you have spoken; for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”
He said, “Please show me your glory.”
He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.”
He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
Yahweh also said, “Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock.
It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and will cover you with my hand until I have passed by;
then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back; but my face shall not be seen.”

footnotes.content: God tells Moses to lead the people toward the Promised Land—the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Notice the inheritance flows through generations, but it rests on a promise older than anyone standing at that moment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An angel will go before them and drive out the nations. God sends an agent rather than walking with them directly—a small kindness wrapped in a large silence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To a land of milk and honey, but God will not be in their midst—they are stiff-necked, and His presence would consume them. Mercy sometimes withdraws closeness to keep us alive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people mourn when they hear the news and remove their jewelry. Their sorrow is real—they have just lost the comfortable sense of God walking with them. Grief can be the first step toward humility.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God calls them stiff-necked again and speaks plainly: His presence would consume them in a moment. He asks them to strip off their jewelry so He might know what to do with them—a quiet way of saying He cannot go forward without a change.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people obey. They strip themselves from that point onward, mourning in the tangible way of removing ornaments. The wilderness will be plainer, but perhaps truer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses pitches the Tent of Meeting outside the camp and calls it by name—a place where anyone seeking God may go. He creates a threshold, a somewhere, where the invisible becomes approachable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whole people watch Moses enter the Tent with focused attention. They stand at their tent doors, watching a man meet with God—a posture of both longing and respect.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cloud pillar descends when Moses enters. His meeting with God draws the presence of God into visibility. The intimacy is also a sign to the waiting people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the people see the pillar stand at the Tent door and rise up to worship at their own tent doors. The public seeing of God's presence awakens worship scattered across the camp.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh speaks to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Joshua, a young man, stays at the Tent after Moses leaves—the next generation drawn to the place of God's presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses lays his burden before God: You tell me to lead them, but You haven't told me whom You'll send with me. Yet you know me by name and I have found favor. He speaks from favor—not from his own worth, but from what God has already shown him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If I have found favor, show me Your way so I may truly know You and find favor in Your sight. Moses asks to see not just what God will do, but who God is. The real request is for intimacy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest. God answers simply—He will go. Rest comes only when God goes. All other provisions are secondary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses holds firm: If Your presence doesn't go with me, don't carry us up from here. He refuses the journey without God. This is the refusal of a man who has tasted the real thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How else will people know I have found favor? If You don't go with us, we are just like all the other nations. Moses sees that God's presence is the only mark that sets them apart. Favor is known by togetherness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will do this thing you have spoken—I know you by name. God grants Moses' plea and repeats that He knows him personally. The request has opened something that cannot now close.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Show me Your glory. A short prayer, almost casual in its boldness—yet it carries a lifetime of walking with God. Moses asks to see what no one can see and live.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will make all my goodness pass before you and proclaim My name. I will be gracious to whom I will, and show mercy on whom I will. God's answer: you will see My goodness and hear My name. Mercy belongs to Him alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You cannot see My face, for man may not see Me and live. Even a granted prayer meets a boundary. Some seeing is not allowed. We live because He holds back His full face.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There is a place by Me, and you shall stand on the rock. God shows Moses a specific place—not a metaphor, but a stone where He will shelter him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: While My glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand. God Himself becomes shelter. To see glory, we must be hidden in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Then I will take away My hand, and you will see My back. Readers today hear an echo here: we too know Christ only in His aftermath—through the empty tomb, the ascension, the sent Spirit. We see His back: we see what He has done, not His face yet. And that is how we live.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
